slides.title: Physics of Agents: Statistical Mechanics Predicts Collective Behavior of AI Agents
slides.tldr: STATISTICAL MECHANICS PREDICTS AI AGENT COLLECTIVE BEHAVIOR
slides.highlight: This research uses a statistical-mechanics formalism to predict collective dynamics like polarization and consensus in LLM-based agent communities, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Statistical mechanics predicts collective AI agent behavior, showing interactions drive conviction and truth-seeking on objective tasks.
card.key_idea: An Ising-model-based formalism where agents update opinions to minimize social pressure, combining intrinsic biases with signed-network interactions (concordant/discordant ties) via a stochastic update rule.
card.evaluation: Simulated >10,000 communities across four LLMs using MATH and political datasets; outperformed Persistence, Interaction-Free, and Mean-Field baselines on held-out questions and unseen graphs.
card.limitation: Subjective questions showed systematic ideological drift toward the right, reflecting underlying language model biases.

slides.title: Insurance as AI Risk Infrastructure: A Generative-Agent Simulation of AI Adoption
slides.highlight: This work uses an LLM-driven agent-based social simulation to analyze how insurance frameworks can mitigate financial risks and accelerate AI adoption, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Insurance accelerates AI adoption by hedging financial risks, reducing bankruptcies and increasing aggregate capital.
card.key_idea: An LLM-driven agent-based social simulation (LABSS) modeling heterogeneous firms that make AI adoption and insurance decisions based on bounded attention and socio-economic behavioral theories.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via mechanism diagnostics and path-level validation across three matched replications; results show 84.38% adoption with insurance versus 74.97% without.

slides.title: Closing the Affective Loop: Multimodal Speaker-Listener Emotion-Dynamics-Aware Empathetic Social Robots
slides.highlight: This work introduces AffectLoop, which tracks speaker verbal and facial affective dynamics alongside the listener's state to improve embodied empathetic interaction. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling within hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: AffectLoop improves robot empathy by conditioning LLM responses on both speaker emotional dynamics and listener states.
card.key_idea: A multimodal pipeline tracking speaker verbal/facial VAD trajectories and robot affective states to generate emotionally congruent spoken responses and embodied behaviors via GPT-4.1-nano.
card.evaluation: Pilot within-subject study (5 participants) comparing AffectLoop to a text-only baseline using Likert scales and interaction-log analysis of affective alignment.
card.limitation: Preliminary results based on a very small sample size of five participants in a pilot study.

slides.title: Pluralistic Human-Robot Interaction: Designing for Robot Interaction with Diverse Communities
slides.tldr: FRAMEWORK FOR INCLUSIVE SOCIAL ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a Pluralistic HRI framework to ensure social robots are designed for diverse communities, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Proposes a Pluralistic HRI framework to treat human diversity as a foundational design concern for social robots.
card.key_idea: A framework integrating seven principles: pluralism, civic dialogue, perspective-taking, empathy, intercultural competence, cultural humility, and moral imagination to create inclusive, adaptive, and ethically grounded interactions.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper outlines proposed evaluation metrics (e.g., inclusion, dialogue quality) rather than reporting results from a specific experiment.
card.limitation: Risks include reinforcing stereotypes, excluding non-normative users, and privileging dominant cultural assumptions if pluralistic principles are not implemented.

slides.title: Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents
slides.highlight: This research analyzes how stubborn agents influence opinion distribution and the time required to reach steady-state in multi-agent networks, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Analyzes how stubborn agents influence opinion convergence in networks using a majority-based 2k-choices update rule.
card.key_idea: Identifies a phase transition in mixing times based on stubborn agent proportions: exponential (sub-critical), logarithmic (super-critical), or polynomial (critical) convergence to steady-state.
card.evaluation: Theoretically derived scaling laws for finite populations were numerically validated by solving forward Kolmogorov and detailed balance equations for mixing times.
card.limitation: The analysis is conducted on a fully connected network, which may not generalize to all graph topologies.

slides.title: Brain-Inspired AI Enables Humanoid Robot to Learn Complex Caregiving Tasks
slides.highlight: This study on brain-inspired AI for humanoid caregiving tasks is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Study Explores Impact on Trust When Expressive Humanoid Robots Make Mistakes
slides.highlight: This study examines how expressive humanoid robots affect human trust when errors occur, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

slides.title: D3D-GEN: Robot-Aware Domain-Grounded Interactive 3D World Generation for Social Robotics
slides.tldr: AUTOMATED 3D WORLD GENERATION FOR SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: D3D-GEN uses a RAG pipeline to automate the creation of interactive 3D simulation environments, supporting the development of embodied AI for social navigation relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: D3D-GEN generates interactive, robot-aware 3D simulation worlds grounded in autonomously retrieved domain-specific knowledge.
card.key_idea: A RAG pipeline using a domain agent to collect real-world constraints, which then guides LLM-based floorplan generation and semantic asset placement for simulators like Isaac Sim.
card.evaluation: Generated 450 worlds across residential, office, and hospital domains; outperformed baselines in object density, visual quality, and VQA accuracy via Gemini-based metrics.
card.limitation: Relies on an existing 3D asset database, which may not be available for every target domain.

slides.title: Leading-Silence Augmentation and Multi-Stage Synthetic Supervision for the Second MLC-SLM Challenge
slides.highlight: This work addresses speaker diarization and recognition in unsegmented multilingual conversations, contributing to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and diarization.

card.one_liner: Improves multilingual conversational speech diarization and understanding using leading-silence augmentation and synthetic QA supervision.
card.key_idea: Task 1 uses random leading-silence cropping and EMA training on VibeVoice-ASR-7B. Task 2 employs synthetic QA generation with silent-audio filtering and distribution-matched augmentation for Qwen3-Omni-30B.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MLC-SLM Challenge sets; Task 1 tcpMER dropped from 18.30% to 16.73%, and Task 2 accuracy rose from 78.0% to 86.0%.
card.limitation: Ablations do not establish robustness to turn-boundary errors or provide per-language and onset-conditioned performance analyses.

slides.title: Learning Varying Physical Therapist-Patient Interactions for Robot-mediated Upper Limb Task-Specific Training
slides.tldr: LEARNING PERSONALIZED THERAPIST-PATIENT INTERACTIONS FOR REHABILITATION ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This research proposes a Learning-from-Demonstration framework to map patient kinematics to therapist torques, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A framework for robots to learn and generalize personalized therapist-patient physical interactions across varying task conditions.
card.key_idea: Uses Task-Parameterised Gaussian Mixture Models (TPGMM) to map patient joint kinematics to therapist-applied torques, generalizing from few demonstrations to unseen task variations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated with 14 mock therapist-patient pairs across three tasks. TPGMM slightly outperformed a Look-Up Table (LUT) benchmark in reconstructing torques for unseen variations.

slides.title: Hippocratic AI rolls out platform to coordinate teams of conversational voice AI agents
slides.tldr: COORDINATION OF CONVERSATIONAL VOICE AI AGENTS
slides.highlight: This platform for coordinating teams of conversational voice AI agents is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

slides.title: Locomotion Variability and User Experience in Smart Wheelchair Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that preserving natural movement variability in shared control for smart wheelchairs improves perceived agency and usefulness. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Preserving natural movement variability in smart wheelchair assistance improves user agency and experience without compromising performance.
card.key_idea: An autonomy-supportive shared control strategy that uses an inverted bell-shaped variability factor to reduce assistance in task-irrelevant areas while maintaining guidance at critical points.
card.evaluation: User study with 18 participants pushing an intelligent powered wheelchair; evaluated via ANOVA on trajectory variance, endpoint error, and subjective questionnaires (SoA, QUEAD2, UEQ).

slides.title: Multi-Agent AI Systems: How Startups Are Building Teams of AI Agents in 2026
slides.highlight: This exploration of startups building teams of AI agents relates to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation using LLM-based agent models.

slides.title: DuplexGen: Decoupling Content, Timing, and Acoustics for Synthetic Dialogue Speech
slides.tldr: SYNTHETIC DIALOGUE FRAMEWORK FOR NATURAL CONVERSATIONAL TIMING
slides.highlight: DuplexGen enables the generation of synthetic conversational speech with emergent timing, interruptions, and overlaps, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: DuplexGen decouples dialogue content, timing, and acoustics to synthesize realistic, interaction-driven conversational speech.
card.key_idea: An LLM generates scripts, two full-duplex models perform them via real-time interaction to emerge timing, and a TTS system re-renders the result with high fidelity.
card.evaluation: Compared against stitching baselines using PriMock57; showed closer FTO distributions and validated ASR stress-tests with Whisper and wav2vec2. Results appear trustworthy.
card.limitation: Lacks mid-utterance interruptions and dynamic content adaptation (e.g., repairs) because dialogue content is fixed before the interaction stage.
